newsitem.title: USA: Korea Development Bank debt deal termed blowout.
newsitem.headline: Korea Development Bank debt deal termed blowout.

text.p: Global investors gave an enthusiastic reception to a $500 million bond offering from the Korea Development Bank (KDB), syndicate officials said.
Thursday's deal was the first to come to market since Korea was invited to join the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) in October.

"The reason this deal did so well is that since Korea has been invited to join the OECD, a number of new investors have been willing to buy these bonds," said John Massad, head of debt syndication at J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.
J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch & Co Inc co-lead-managed the $500 million global offering of 6.625 percent bonds due 2003.

The bonds priced at a 49-basis-point spread to the seven-year Treasury. That price was far more aggressive than a $750 million 10-year deal from KDB that priced at 74 basis points over the 10-year Treasury last May, he said.
Massad said KDB investors will received tangible benefits if the Korean parliament approves Korea's entry into the OECD.

He said if Korea becomes an OECD country, the risk weighting of KDB debt will be reduced to zero percent from 100 percent by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), making the paper more economical for financial institutions to hold as an investment.
As a result, Massad said the deal saw strong demand from European buyers, particularly banks, which purchased approximately 40 percent of the deal.
In the U.S., the offering attracted a number of new investors such as insurance companies, he said.
